headline: SILVER DIPS BELOW $75 AS U.S. TARGETS IRANIAN DRONES — Ceasefire Optimism Hammers Haven Demand
snippet: Silver opened lower Thursday after U.S. forces struck Iranian drones overnight and ceasefire optimism drained safe-haven demand. Silver has now fallen from a wartime peak near $87 to below $75 — a 14% drawdown — as U.S.-Iran peace talks edge toward a Strait of Hormuz agreement. Gold slipped to ~$4,400 on May 27 before partially recovering to $4,456.

headline: ACID CRUNCH: Iran War Doubles Sulphuric Acid Prices — 42% of Nickel Costs and Half of Global Battery Metal Output Now at Risk
snippet: Benchmark Mineral Intelligence warns sulphur prices have climbed more than 50% since the Iran conflict began, with sulphuric acid doubling in some regions. Sulphur now accounts for 42% of HPAL nickel production costs (up from 26%) and has surpassed energy as lithium's largest single C1 cost component. Spot acid in Indonesia and Chile has exceeded $380–$440/tonne as converters scramble for alternatives.

headline: U.S. LOCKS IN GREENLAND RARE EARTH SUPPLY: REalloys Signs 15-Year Tanbreez Offtake Ahead of Pentagon's 2027 Chinese Materials Ban
snippet: REalloys (ALOY) secured a definitive 15-year offtake covering 15% of Phase 1 production from Critical Metals Corp.'s (CRML) Tanbreez project in Greenland — one of the world's largest heavy rare earth deposits, rich in Dysprosium and Terbium used in fighter aircraft and missile systems. The deal is positioned as a direct supply chain response to the Pentagon's 2027 ban on Chinese-origin rare earth materials.

headline: MERDEKA GOLD REVIVES A DEAD LISTING TYPE — $500M Hong Kong HDR Float Targets June, First Such Listing in 12 Years
snippet: Indonesia's Merdeka Gold Resources plans to raise at least $500 million in Hong Kong via depositary receipts as early as June — rebooting an instrument (HDR) not seen on HKEX in 12 years. Shares in the Jakarta-listed company have surged 151% since its September 2025 IPO, driven by its Pani mine in Gorontalo, Indonesia's largest primary gold project with 7Moz in resources targeting 500,000 oz/yr by 2032.

headline: STRIKEPOINT GOLD DRILLS BEST-EVER HOLE AT NEVADA'S HERCULES — 114m at 0.69 g/t Au Opens Oxide Heap-Leach Zone
snippet: StrikePoint Gold's spring drill program in Nevada's Walker Lane returned hole H26-004: 114.30m at 0.69 g/t Au and 5.03 g/t Ag from 135.64m, including 9.14m at 2.95 g/t Au — the best grade-width intercept in the project's history. The dominantly oxide mineralisation opens the potential for a heap-leach operation similar to other Nevada producers. A maiden resource estimate is targeted for Q4 2026.

headline: NEWMONT VS. SSR MINING: Analyst Picks a Winner as Gold Stocks Still Trade at a Discount to the Metal
snippet: With gold near $4,450/oz but mining equities still lagging the metal, a Motley Fool analyst squares off Newmont's diversified Tier-1 portfolio against SSR Mining's leaner structure. The piece argues the persistent valuation gap between gold stocks and bullion is the key opportunity of 2026 — with operational cost discipline as the deciding factor for which company closes it first.

headline: TROILUS WEST RIM DRILLING SPARKS TAKEOVER TALK — Red Cloud Sees High-Grade Satellite Forming Near Quebec Pit
snippet: Red Cloud Securities analyst Ron Stewart says new West Rim intercepts — including 19m at 2.69 g/t Au within 200m of the reserve pit — reinforce the case for a high-grade satellite at Troilus. With US$1.3B in export credit pledges from Germany, Finland, and Canada, and a construction decision targeted this year, the Quebec project is increasingly seen as a takeover candidate.

headline: NSW INCHES CLOSER TO LIFTING 40-YEAR URANIUM BAN — Bill Advances from Upper House to Legislative Assembly
snippet: New South Wales' Legislative Council passed the Uranium Mining and Nuclear Facilities (Prohibitions) Repeal Bill, which now heads to the Legislative Assembly. Passage would lift a prohibition in place since 1986, opening Australia's most populous state to uranium exploration and extraction for the first time in four decades — with significant implications for the global uranium supply chain.

headline: CHINA IMPORTS 790+ TONNES OF SILVER IN EARLY 2026 — Sixth Consecutive Year of Market Deficit Deepens
snippet: China's silver imports hit 790+ tonnes in the first months of 2026, driven by solar panel manufacturing and EV production. Silver is entering its sixth consecutive annual deficit as record industrial demand outpaces flat mine supply — a structural underpinning that persists despite short-term price pressure from Iran ceasefire optimism.

headline: COPPER CONSOLIDATES FROM $6.65 RECORD AS SECTION 232 TARIFF DECISION LOOMS — Goldman Sees 25%+ Duty Near-Certain Before Mid-June
snippet: Copper hit an all-time high of $6.65/lb on May 13 before easing to $6.34/lb as Iran ceasefire optimism eased fears about sulphur supply disruptions. Goldman Sachs assigns high probability to a U.S. refined copper tariff of at least 25% before mid-June, a decision that would widen the COMEX-LME spread by $0.30–0.80/lb and accelerate capital into North American copper developers ahead of a projected 600,000-tonne 2026 deficit.
